Consult Summary:
- Adult male with acute central chest pressure and dyspnea; high suspicion for acute coronary syndrome (ACS). EMS activated for urgent hospital evaluation.

History:
- Presenting complaint/timeline: Sudden-onset central chest discomfort/pressure beginning a few hours prior to consult; persistent at ~7/10 without improvement.
- Character/location/radiation: Midline pressure “like someone sitting on my chest”; radiates to left shoulder/arm; not to head or back.
- Associated symptoms: Shortness of breath, light-headedness, nausea (no vomiting). Reports recent exertional dyspnea (stairs/hills). Notes calf pain and leg swelling.
- Pertinent negatives: No dysphagia; no problems with urination; no vomiting; no back radiation; no head radiation.
- Past medical history: Hypertension; hypercholesterolemia.
- Medications: None.
- Allergies: Not documented.
- Social: Smoker; lives with wife.
- Context: Conflicting reports on activity at onset (initially while digging/gardening; later states he had been relaxing/watching TV but also mentions going into the garden).

Examination:
- Setting: Telehealth; no vitals obtained.
- Exam/observations: Not performed. Patient reports ongoing chest pressure and dyspnea during call.

Impression:
- Working diagnosis: Acute Coronary Syndrome (possible MI or unstable angina) — high suspicion.
  - Supporting: Sudden persistent central pressure with left arm radiation; exertional association; dyspnea, light-headedness, nausea; cardiovascular risk factors (HTN, hyperlipidemia, smoking); not on cardioprotective medications.
- Additional considerations:
  - Pulmonary embolism — moderate consideration given acute dyspnea with reported calf pain and leg swelling; chest pressure less typical than pleuritic pain.
  - Aortic dissection — low likelihood (no tearing pain, back radiation, or neurologic signs reported).

Plan:
- Emergency management: EMS/ambulance called for urgent transport to hospital.
- Interim advice: Remain calm; sip water as needed; avoid taking any medications before EMS arrival.
- Hospital evaluation: Paramedics to assess cardiac and respiratory status; expedited ED/consultant assessment on arrival.
- Support: Inform wife and prepare for hospital visit.
- Follow-up: Clinician to arrange follow-up after hospital assessment.

Quality checks:
● Missing elements:
  - Allergies not confirmed.
  - Full medication list not reviewed beyond “none.”
  - Family history, surgical history, and detailed social history (alcohol, drugs, occupational risks) not obtained.
  - Vitals and physical exam absent (telehealth context).
  - Specific ED workup details and final disposition not documented.
● Conflicts between transcript and DDx:
  - Onset context: Initially reported onset during gardening; later stated he was relaxing/watching TV before onset but also referenced going into the garden (conflict noted). DDx assumes exertional onset; transcript contains both accounts.
  - Minor communication mismatch when asked about ongoing discomfort; patient responded about smoking, but later confirmed ongoing chest pressure.
● Transcript quality:
  - Some incomplete/inaudible segments and overlapping dialogue; minor inconsistencies in timeline. Overall sufficient to justify urgent ACS evaluation.
